name: Nuclear Chemistry
tagline: Radioactivity, nuclear reactions, and radiopharmaceutical chemistry.
seo_title: Nuclear Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Nuclear Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in radiochemistry, nuclear medicine, nuclear energy and heavy elements.

definition.lead: Nuclear chemistry studies radioactivity, nuclear reactions and the chemistry of radioactive elements.
definition.body: It made possible nuclear power, radiocarbon dating, and medical imaging and therapy with radioisotopes. It also deals with the heaviest elements, nuclear waste and radioactivity in the environment.

timeline.title: Radioactivity
timeline.text: Henri Becquerel finds that uranium salts expose photographic plates.

timeline.title: Polonium and radium
timeline.text: Marie and Pierre Curie discover two new radioactive elements.
timeline.why: Radioactivity became a tool for finding elements.

timeline.title: Marie Curie's second Nobel Prize
timeline.text: She receives the Chemistry prize for polonium and radium.
timeline.why: The first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.

timeline.title: Artificial radioactivity
timeline.text: Irène and Frédéric Joliot-Curie make radioactive isotopes by bombarding elements.
timeline.why: Radioisotopes could be made on demand.

timeline.title: Nuclear fission
timeline.text: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann detect barium from uranium; Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explain it as fission.

timeline.title: The first transuranium element
timeline.text: Edwin McMillan and Philip Abelson make neptunium.
timeline.why: Beyond uranium on the periodic table.

timeline.title: Radiocarbon dating
timeline.why: A clock for the last tens of thousands of years.

timeline.title: PET imaging with FDG
timeline.text: A fluorine-18 labelled glucose is first used in humans.

timeline.title: Element 118 named
timeline.why: The heaviest element named so far.
